easy.feedback: With money demand fixed, the larger money supply moves equilibrium down MD0 from 4 percent to 2 percent.
easy.imageAlt: Money-market diagram with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1.
easy.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is quantity of money and the vertical axis is nominal interest rate. The straight downward MD0 line runs from (0,12) to (150,0). Solid MS0 is vertical at quantity 100; its MD0 intersection is at rate 4. Dashed MS1 is vertical at quantity 125; its MD0 intersection is at rate 2. Horizontal dashed guides mark rates 4 and 2.

easy.q: When the money-supply line moves left from 100 to 75, how does the equilibrium interest rate respond?
options: It rises from 4 percent to 6 percent
It falls from 6 percent to 4 percent
It stays at 4 percent
It rises from 2 percent to 4 percent
easy.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
easy.feedback: With money demand fixed, the smaller money supply moves equilibrium up MD0 from 4 percent to 6 percent.
easy.imageAlt: Money-market diagram with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1.
easy.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is quantity of money and the vertical axis is nominal interest rate. The straight downward MD0 line runs from (0,12) to (150,0). Solid MS0 is vertical at quantity 100; its MD0 intersection is at rate 4. Dashed MS1 is vertical at quantity 75; its MD0 intersection is at rate 6. Horizontal dashed guides mark rates 4 and 6.

easy.q: Which labeled point is the original equilibrium where MD0 intersects MS0?
options: Point A
Point C
Point B
Point D
easy.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
easy.feedback: The original curves MD0 and MS0 intersect at point B, quantity 75 and interest rate 3.
easy.imageAlt: Money-market diagram with two vertical MS lines, two downward MD lines and labeled points A, B, C and D.
easy.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is quantity of money; the vertical axis is nominal interest rate. Solid MS0 is vertical at 75 and dashed MS1 at 100. Solid MD0 is the lower straight downward line, through B (75,3) and D (100,1). Dashed MD1 is the upper parallel line, through A (75,6) and C (100,4). MD1 crosses the vertical axis at 12 and the horizontal axis at 150. MD0 crosses the vertical axis at 9. All four points are marked with black dots.

easy.q: In the left panel, money demand rises from MD0 to MD1 while MS0 stays fixed. What happens to the nominal interest rate?
options: It rises from 2 percent to 4 percent
It falls from 4 percent to 2 percent
It stays at 2 percent
It rises from 4 percent to 6 percent
easy.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
easy.feedback: With fixed money supply, the higher money-demand curve raises the equilibrium interest rate from point A to point B.
easy.imageAlt: Two panels with MS0, MD0 and MD1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
easy.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. MS0 is vertical at 75. Solid downward MD0 passes through A (75,2); upper dashed MD1 passes through B (75,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and lower dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 and SRAS meet at A (150,55); AD1 and SRAS meet at B (105,45). Dashed guides identify the point coordinates.

medium.q: Refer to the money-market graph. With MD1 unchanged, money supply increases from MS1 to MS2. Which equilibrium movement follows?
options: g to e
e to g
a to d
c to f
medium.commonError: Using the wrong money demand curve.
medium.feedback: MD1 intersects MS1 at e and MS2 at g. Increasing supply moves equilibrium from e to g and lowers the nominal interest rate.
medium.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
medium.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

medium.q: Refer to the money-market graph. If money demand shifts from MD1 to MD2 while money supply remains MS1, equilibrium moves from:
options: e to a
a to e
g to d
f to c
medium.commonError: Confusing money demand shifts with money supply shifts.
medium.feedback: At MS1, MD1 intersects at e and MD2 intersects at a, so the interest rate rises.
medium.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
medium.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

medium.q: Refer to the money-market graph. Which point shows MS2 and MD2 in equilibrium?
options: a
b
d
g
medium.commonError: Reading a non-intersection point as equilibrium.
medium.feedback: MS2 and MD2 intersect at point d.
medium.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
medium.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

medium.q: If real income rises, money demand increases. In the liquidity preference model, this tends to:
options: Raise the interest rate
Lower the interest rate
Reduce money supply automatically
Shift AD left directly
medium.commonError: Thinking more money demand lowers interest rates.
medium.feedback: Higher money demand pushes the interest rate up when money supply is fixed.

medium.q: Liquidity preference theory explains the interest rate as the variable that balances
options: money supply and money demand
labor supply and labor demand
exports and imports
taxes and spending
medium.commonError: confusing money market equilibrium with AD-AS equilibrium
medium.feedback: The interest rate adjusts to balance money supply and money demand.

medium.q: Which curve shows the amount of money fixed by the central bank?
options: The vertical money supply curve
The downward-sloping money demand curve
The aggregate demand curve
The multiplier curve
medium.commonError: thinking money demand is fixed by the central bank
medium.feedback: The central bank fixes the money supply in this model, so money supply is vertical.

want fewer goods and services
face a lower price level automatically
stop holding liquid assets

need fewer dollars to buy the same goods
earn no income

Money demand falls, interest rates fall, and investment rises.
Money supply rises, interest rates fall, and AD shifts right.
Money demand rises, interest rates fall, and investment rises.

hard.feedback: Higher prices increase money demand, which raises interest rates and reduces investment.

hard.q: Why does a lower price level increase the quantity of goods and services demanded?
options: Lower prices reduce money demand, lower interest rates, and increase investment.
Lower prices increase money demand, raise interest rates, and lower investment.
Lower prices reduce money supply and shift AD left.
Lower prices eliminate the need for investment.
hard.commonError: thinking lower prices raise money demand
hard.feedback: Lower prices reduce money demand, which lowers interest rates and raises investment spending.

hard.q: If money demand shifts right while money supply stays fixed, what must happen to restore money-market equilibrium?
options: The interest rate rises.
The interest rate falls.
Money supply shifts left automatically.
Aggregate demand becomes vertical.

hard.feedback: With fixed money supply, stronger money demand pushes the equilibrium interest rate up.

hard.q: A rise in real income shifts money demand right. If the Fed holds money supply fixed, what happens next?
options: Interest rates rise.
Interest rates fall.
Money supply rises automatically.
Investment rises because borrowing is cheaper.
hard.commonError: thinking higher income lowers transaction demand for money
hard.feedback: Higher income increases money demand. With fixed money supply, the interest rate rises.

hard.q: A fall in the price level shifts money demand left. If money supply is fixed, what happens to the interest rate?
options: It falls.
It rises.
It stays fixed because money demand cannot shift.
It becomes the inflation rate.
hard.commonError: thinking a lower price level increases money demand
hard.feedback: A lower price level reduces the dollars needed for transactions, so money demand falls and interest rates fall.

hard.q: Moving downward along MD0 from a higher to a lower interest rate, what happens to the quantity of money demanded?

The quantity of money supplied rises.
The money-demand curve shifts left.
The quantity of money demanded rises.

elite.q: If income rises and the Fed prevents interest rates from rising, what policy shift is needed?
options: Increase money supply as money demand rises
Decrease money supply as money demand rises
Increase money demand as money supply falls
Decrease money demand as interest rates rise
elite.commonError: Forgetting the Fed must offset higher money demand.
elite.feedback: Higher income raises money demand; to hold rates down, the Fed must increase money supply.

elite.q: If the Fed cuts money supply while money demand rises, what happens to the interest rate pressure?
options: It rises from both forces
It falls from both forces
It rises from supply but falls from demand
It falls from supply but rises from demand
elite.commonError: Missing that both shifts raise rates.
elite.feedback: Lower money supply and higher money demand both push the interest rate upward.

elite.q: Starting in money-market equilibrium, the price level rises. Which full chain explains the interest-rate effect on aggregate demand?
options: Higher P raises money demand, raises r, lowers investment, and lowers quantity of goods and services demanded.
Higher P lowers money demand, lowers r, raises investment, and raises quantity demanded.
Higher P raises money supply, lowers r, raises investment, and shifts AD right.
Higher P lowers money supply, raises r, and shifts money demand left.
elite.commonError: reversing the price-level effect on money demand
elite.feedback: Higher prices require more money for transactions. That raises money demand, raises interest rates, lowers investment, and reduces quantity demanded.

elite.q: Starting at P1 and r1, the price level falls to P2. What happens in the money market and AD model?
options: Money demand falls, r falls, investment rises, and output demanded rises.
Money demand rises, r rises, investment falls, and output demanded falls.
Money supply falls, r rises, and AD shifts left.
Money demand falls, r rises, and investment falls.
elite.commonError: thinking lower prices increase money demand
elite.feedback: A lower price level reduces money demand, lowers interest rates, raises investment, and increases quantity demanded.

elite.q: Money demand shifts from MD1 to MD2 while money supply remains fixed. What is the likely effect on r and investment?
options: r rises and investment falls.
r falls and investment rises.
r rises and investment rises.
r falls and investment falls.
elite.commonError: thinking higher money demand lowers the interest rate
elite.feedback: With fixed money supply, a rightward shift in money demand raises the interest rate, which lowers investment.

elite.q: Money demand shifts left while money supply remains fixed. What chain follows?
options: r falls, investment rises, and AD tends to increase.
r rises, investment falls, and AD tends to decrease.
r falls, investment falls, and AD tends to decrease.
r rises, investment rises, and AD tends to increase.
elite.commonError: missing the investment response after the money-market movement
elite.feedback: Lower money demand reduces the equilibrium interest rate, which supports investment and AD.

elite.q: If a rise in the price level shifts money demand right and the Fed does not change money supply, why does this help explain the downward slope of AD?
options: Higher P raises r and lowers investment, reducing quantity demanded.
Higher P lowers r and raises investment, increasing quantity demanded.
Higher P shifts AD right by increasing investment.
Higher P makes money supply rise automatically.
elite.commonError: missing that this is movement along AD, not an AD shift
elite.feedback: Higher P raises money demand and interest rates, lowering investment and quantity demanded along the AD curve.

elite.q: If an increase in Y raises money demand and the Fed wants to prevent r from rising, what should the Fed do?
options: Increase money supply to match the higher money demand.
Decrease money supply to reduce money demand.
Raise taxes because money supply cannot shift.
Reduce government spending to make MD vertical.
elite.commonError: thinking the Fed should reduce money supply when money demand rises
elite.feedback: If money demand rises, increasing money supply can prevent the equilibrium interest rate from rising.

elite.q: If P rises, money demand shifts right. If the Fed also increases money supply enough to hold r constant, what happens to the interest-rate effect on AD?
options: It is offset because r does not rise to reduce investment.
It becomes stronger because r rises more.
It reverses because investment must fall more.
It disappears because AD is no longer related to spending.
elite.commonError: ignoring that Fed policy can offset money-demand pressure on r
elite.feedback: If the Fed accommodates the higher money demand, r does not rise, so the investment channel behind the interest-rate effect is muted.

elite.q: A student says a fall in the interest rate from 8 percent to 6 percent would shift MD0 to the right. What is the best correction?

Interest-rate changes shift MD0 because the rate is on the axis.
Interest-rate changes shift MS0 while MD0 stays fixed.
Interest-rate changes shift both MD0 and MS0 together.
elite.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
elite.feedback: The interest rate is the price variable on the money-demand curve. Changing it moves the economy along MD0.

MD0 shifts right while money supply remains fixed at MS0 throughout.
MD0 and money supply both shift left to separate new curves.
Neither money demand nor money supply changes in the diagram.

Interest rates fall because higher income lowers money demand.
Interest rates stay fixed because money demand cannot shift.
Interest rates fall because fixed money supply means more lending.

legendary.q: Money demand rises while the Fed increases money supply. Which conclusion is safest?
options: The interest-rate effect is ambiguous without knowing relative shift sizes.
Interest rates must rise because money demand always dominates.
Interest rates must fall because money supply always dominates.
Interest rates must stay fixed because both curves shifted.
legendary.commonError: Assuming one shift always dominates.
legendary.feedback: When money demand and money supply both increase, the interest-rate effect depends on which shift is larger.

legendary.q: Money demand rises because income rises, while the Fed cuts the money supply. Which memo is strongest?
options: Both forces push interest rates upward and pressure AD downward.
Both forces push interest rates downward and pressure AD upward.
Money demand raises rates, but lower money supply lowers rates.
Money demand lowers rates, but lower money supply raises rates.
legendary.commonError: Missing that both shifts raise interest rates.
legendary.feedback: Higher money demand and lower money supply both raise interest rates, weakening investment and AD.

legendary.q: Money demand falls while the Fed expands money supply. Which memo is strongest?
options: Both forces push interest rates downward and support AD.
Both forces push interest rates upward and weaken AD.
Money demand lowers rates, but higher money supply raises rates.
Money demand raises rates, but higher money supply lowers rates.
legendary.commonError: Missing that both shifts lower interest rates.
legendary.feedback: Lower money demand and higher money supply both push interest rates down, supporting investment and AD.

legendary.q: Money demand shifts right while money supply is fixed. If the Fed wants to prevent the resulting interest-rate increase, what should it do?
options: Increase money supply enough to offset the rightward money-demand shift.
Decrease money supply to reinforce the money-demand shift.
Raise taxes because taxes directly shift money demand left.
Do nothing because r must fall when money demand rises.
legendary.commonError: thinking the Fed should reduce money supply when money demand rises
legendary.feedback: A rightward money-demand shift raises r if MS is fixed. Increasing MS can offset that pressure.

legendary.q: Real income rises and the central bank increases the money supply enough to leave the equilibrium interest rate unchanged. What must be true?
options: Money demand stayed fixed even though higher income increased transaction volume.
The money supply shifted left by enough to offset the rise in money demand.
The price level fell to zero and eliminated the need to hold transaction balances.
The money-supply increase offset the rise in money demand.
legendary.commonError: Assuming an unchanged interest rate means neither curve shifted.
legendary.feedback: Higher income raises money demand. A sufficiently large increase in money supply can offset that pressure and leave the equilibrium interest rate unchanged.

legendary.q: If the nominal interest rate were temporarily above point A while MS0 stayed fixed, what adjustment pressure would the graph imply?
options: Excess money demand pushes the rate farther above A.
Excess money supply pushes the rate down toward A.
Money supply shifts right until the rate rises above A.
Money demand shifts left until the rate remains above A.
legendary.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
legendary.feedback: Above equilibrium, the quantity of money demanded is less than the fixed money supply. Portfolio adjustment pushes the interest rate back down toward equilibrium.
legendary.imageAlt: Money market with downward-sloping money demand MD0 and vertical money supply MS0 intersecting at point A.
legendary.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is quantity of money and the vertical axis is nominal interest rate. Money demand MD0 slopes downward from an interest rate of 12 at quantity 0 to 0 at quantity 200. Money supply MS0 is vertical at quantity 100. The curves intersect at point A, quantity of money 100 and nominal interest rate 6.

legendary.q: Starting from the money-market change shown, which downstream effect would normally follow?
options: Lower rates cut interest-sensitive spending and shift AD left.
Higher rates raise interest-sensitive spending and shift AD right.
Higher rates cut interest-sensitive spending and shift AD left.
Lower rates raise interest-sensitive spending and shift AD right.
legendary.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
legendary.feedback: The standard transmission channel runs from more money to lower interest rates to more interest-sensitive spending and higher aggregate demand.
legendary.imageAlt: Money-market diagram with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1.
legendary.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is quantity of money and the vertical axis is nominal interest rate. The straight downward MD0 line runs from (0,12) to (150,0). Solid MS0 is vertical at quantity 100; its MD0 intersection is at rate 4. Dashed MS1 is vertical at quantity 125; its MD0 intersection is at rate 2. Horizontal dashed guides mark rates 4 and 2.

legendary.q: After the money-supply change from MS0 to MS1 shown in the graph, which spending-and-AD response should follow?
options: Higher rates raise interest-sensitive spending and shift AD right.
Higher rates cut interest-sensitive spending and shift AD left.
Lower rates cut interest-sensitive spending and shift AD left.
Lower rates raise interest-sensitive spending and shift AD right.
legendary.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
legendary.feedback: The standard contractionary chain runs from less money to higher interest rates to less interest-sensitive spending and lower aggregate demand.
legendary.imageAlt: Money-market diagram with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1.
legendary.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is quantity of money and the vertical axis is nominal interest rate. The straight downward MD0 line runs from (0,12) to (150,0). Solid MS0 is vertical at quantity 100; its MD0 intersection is at rate 4. Dashed MS1 is vertical at quantity 75; its MD0 intersection is at rate 6. Horizontal dashed guides mark rates 4 and 6.

legendary.q: Refer to the graph. The economy starts at B with MD0 and MS0. Money demand changes to MD1. The central bank increases money supply to MS1, but wants to restore B’s original nominal interest rate. If the straight MD1 line continues as drawn, approximately how much additional money beyond MS1 is needed?
options: 25 units; a total money quantity of 125.
No additional money; C already restores the original rate.
75 units; a total money quantity of 175.
12.5 units; a total money quantity of 112.5.
legendary.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
legendary.feedback: B’s rate is 3. MD1 passes through A at (75,6) and C at (100,4), a fall of 2 rate points per 25 money units. A further 1-point fall requires 12.5 additional units, beyond MS1 at 100.
legendary.imageAlt: Money-market diagram with two vertical MS lines, two downward MD lines and labeled points A, B, C and D.
legendary.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is quantity of money; the vertical axis is nominal interest rate. Solid MS0 is vertical at 75 and dashed MS1 at 100. Solid MD0 is the lower straight downward line, through B (75,3) and D (100,1). Dashed MD1 is the upper parallel line, through A (75,6) and C (100,4). MD1 crosses the vertical axis at 12 and the horizontal axis at 150. MD0 crosses the vertical axis at 9. All four points are marked with black dots.

legendary.q: Which complete chain is consistent with the two-panel graph?
options: MD ↑; rate ↓; interest-sensitive spending ↑; AD →; GDP and prices ↑.
MD ↑; rate ↑; interest-sensitive spending ↓; AD ←; GDP and prices ↓.
MS ↑; rate ↑; interest-sensitive spending ↓; AD ←; GDP and prices ↑.
MD ↓; rate ↑; interest-sensitive spending ↑; AD →; GDP and prices ↑.
legendary.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
legendary.feedback: The panels show the full liquidity-preference transmission from a money-demand increase to a higher rate and lower aggregate demand.
legendary.imageAlt: Two panels with MS0, MD0 and MD1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
legendary.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. MS0 is vertical at 75. Solid downward MD0 passes through A (75,2); upper dashed MD1 passes through B (75,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and lower dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 and SRAS meet at A (150,55); AD1 and SRAS meet at B (105,45). Dashed guides identify the point coordinates.

legendary.q: Refer to the money-market graph. Starting at point e (MS1 with MD1), both money demand and money supply shift right to MD2 and MS2. The new equilibrium is point d. What does the change from r2 to r3 imply?
options: The rightward money-demand shift exerts more upward pressure on the interest rate than the rightward money-supply shift offsets.
The money-supply shift must have dominated because any increase in money supply mechanically raises interest rates more than a simultaneous money-demand shift can affect them.
Both rightward shifts necessarily leave the interest rate unchanged.
The new equilibrium shows that money demand fell relative to money supply.
legendary.commonError: Assumes the direction of one curve shift determines the interest rate even when both money demand and money supply move.
legendary.feedback: When money demand and money supply both shift, compare the new equilibrium with the old one; the interest-rate direction depends on their relative effects.
legendary.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
legendary.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

legendary.q: Refer to the money-market graph. With MD2 and MS2, the equilibrium is point d at r3. If the interest rate is temporarily at point b on MS2 at r4, what adjustment should occur?
options: There is excess money demand, so households sell interest-bearing assets; bond prices fall and the interest rate rises farther above r4 before the market can clear.
Point b is already the equilibrium because it lies on MS2.
Money demand must shift right again before the interest rate can change.
There is excess money supply; people try to buy interest-bearing assets, putting downward pressure on the interest rate toward r3.
legendary.commonError: Treats a labeled point on a money-supply line as an equilibrium even when it is not on the active money-demand curve.
legendary.feedback: At an interest rate above equilibrium, money supplied exceeds money demanded and asset-market adjustment pushes the rate down; below equilibrium, excess money demand pushes it up.
legendary.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
legendary.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

legendary.q: Refer to the money-market graph. With MD1 and MS1, equilibrium is point e at r2. If the interest rate is temporarily at r1, what pressure moves the market back toward equilibrium?
options: The market remains at r1 because a vertical money-supply curve prevents interest-rate adjustment.
The central bank must reduce the fixed money supply before households can obtain enough money balances and the interest rate can move back toward equilibrium.
Quantity of money demanded exceeds the fixed money supply, so attempts to raise money by selling interest-bearing assets put upward pressure on the interest rate.
Quantity of money supplied exceeds money demanded, so asset purchases push the interest rate lower.
legendary.commonError: Treats a labeled point on a money-supply line as an equilibrium even when it is not on the active money-demand curve.
legendary.feedback: At an interest rate above equilibrium, money supplied exceeds money demanded and asset-market adjustment pushes the rate down; below equilibrium, excess money demand pushes it up.
legendary.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
legendary.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

legendary.q: Real income rises while the overall price level falls. With money supply fixed, what can be concluded about the equilibrium interest rate from liquidity-preference theory alone?
options: It cannot change because income and the price level never shift money demand.
The direction is ambiguous because higher income raises money demand while a lower price level reduces money demand.
It must rise because every increase in real income dominates every change in the price level.
It must fall because the price-level effect always dominates the income effect.
legendary.commonError: Assumes the direction of one curve shift determines the interest rate even when both money demand and money supply move.
legendary.feedback: When money demand and money supply both shift, compare the new equilibrium with the old one; the interest-rate direction depends on their relative effects.

legendary.q: The central bank increases the money supply and the equilibrium interest rate falls while income and the price level are unchanged. A student says, “Money demand shifted left.” What is the best correction?
options: The fall in the interest rate is a movement along the existing money-demand curve unless a money-demand shifter also changed.
The student is correct because any fall in interest rates shifts the entire money-demand curve left at every quantity, even when income and the price level are unchanged.
Money demand shifts right whenever money supply increases.
Money demand becomes horizontal after an expansionary money-supply change.
legendary.commonError: Calls an interest-rate-induced movement along a money-demand curve a shift of the curve.
legendary.feedback: A change in the interest rate causes movement along a given money-demand curve. Income or the price level can shift the money-demand curve.

legendary.q: Refer to the money-market graph. The economy begins at e with MD1 and MS1. Money demand shifts to MD2, and the central bank also expands money supply to MS2. Is the increase in money supply large enough to keep the interest rate at r2?
options: Yes. Any rightward money-supply shift exactly offsets any rightward money-demand shift.
Yes. Point d lies on MS2, so the interest rate must still equal r2.
No. The central bank would need to reduce money supply to keep the interest rate from rising.
No. The new equilibrium d is at r3, so the central bank would need a larger rightward money-supply shift to hold the rate at r2.
legendary.commonError: Uses a contractionary money-supply response to offset a rightward money-demand shift.
legendary.feedback: If money demand shifts right and the central bank wants to prevent the interest rate from rising, it must increase money supply enough to accommodate the higher demand.
legendary.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
legendary.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

legendary.q: Real income rises, shifting money demand right, yet the observed equilibrium interest rate falls. Which inference is most consistent with the liquidity-preference model?
options: Money demand could not have risen because income never affects transaction demand.
The central bank must have held money supply fixed because a fixed supply guarantees a lower rate.
Money supply must have increased enough to more than offset the upward interest-rate pressure from higher money demand.
Money supply must have fallen because lower supply always lowers interest rates.
legendary.commonError: Ignores the opposing pressure from a money-demand increase when interpreting a falling interest rate.
legendary.feedback: If money demand rises but the equilibrium interest rate falls, money supply must have risen by enough to more than offset the upward interest-rate pressure from money demand.

boss.q: In liquidity preference theory, the interest rate balances which two quantities?
options: money supply and money demand
taxes and government spending
exports and imports
labor supply and labor demand
boss.commonError: confusing money market equilibrium with AD-AS equilibrium
boss.feedback: The interest rate balances money supply and money demand.

boss.q: If the price level rises, what happens in the money market?
options: Money demand rises and interest rates rise.
Money demand falls and interest rates fall.
Money supply rises and interest rates fall.
Money supply falls and interest rates fall.
boss.commonError: thinking higher prices reduce money demand
boss.feedback: Higher prices mean people need more money for transactions, so money demand rises and interest rates rise.

boss.q: A higher price level raises money demand, interest rates rise, and investment falls by $40 billion. If MPC = 0.75, what is the total AD decrease from this channel?
options: $160 billion
$40 billion
$53.3 billion
$30 billion
boss.commonError: using MPC instead of the multiplier
boss.feedback: MPC 0.75 gives multiplier 4. A $40 billion investment fall reduces AD by $160 billion.

boss.q: In the liquidity-preference model, the opportunity cost of holding money is the:
options: Interest income forgone by not holding interest-bearing assets.
The current price level paid for goods and services during the year.
The required reserve ratio applied to deposits held by commercial banks.
The previous year’s inflation rate reported by the statistical agency.
boss.commonError: Confusing the opportunity cost of money with a price index or reserve rule.
boss.feedback: Holding money sacrifices the interest that could have been earned on bonds or other interest-bearing assets.

boss.q: If the money supply increases while money demand is unchanged, the equilibrium interest rate tends to:
options: Rise.
Fall.
Remain fixed by definition.
Become equal to the inflation rate.
boss.commonError: Reversing the interest-rate effect of a rightward money-supply shift.
boss.feedback: More money supplied at each interest rate creates excess money balances until the interest rate falls.

boss.q: Which event shifts money demand to the right?
options: An open-market purchase that increases money supply.
A decrease in the amount of currency printed.
An increase in real income and transactions.
A lower required reserve ratio by itself.
boss.commonError: Selecting a money-supply event as a money-demand shifter.
boss.feedback: Higher income generates more transactions and raises the quantity of money people want to hold at each interest rate.

boss.q: The price level rises while the nominal money supply is fixed. What happens in the money market?
options: Money demand falls and the equilibrium interest rate decreases.
Money supply rises and the equilibrium interest rate decreases.
Both curves remain fixed because only prices changed.
Money demand rises and the equilibrium interest rate increases.
boss.commonError: Ignoring the transaction-money demand created by a higher price level.
boss.feedback: A higher price level increases nominal transaction needs, shifting money demand right and raising the interest rate with fixed supply.

boss.q: The central bank increases the money supply. Through the interest-rate effect, what happens next?
options: The interest rate falls, encouraging investment and aggregate demand.
The interest rate rises, reducing investment and aggregate demand.
The price level falls before the interest rate changes.
Money demand shifts left because reserves increased.
boss.commonError: Reversing the monetary-policy transmission chain.
boss.feedback: A larger money supply lowers the equilibrium interest rate, which tends to increase interest-sensitive spending.

boss.q: Real income falls while the money supply is fixed. What is the likely equilibrium change?
options: Money demand rises and the interest rate increases.
Money demand falls and the interest rate decreases.
Money supply falls and the interest rate increases.
Money demand is unchanged because income is real.
boss.commonError: Reversing the money-demand response to lower transaction volume.
boss.feedback: Lower real income reduces transactions, shifts money demand left, and lowers the equilibrium interest rate.

legendaryBoss.q: Money demand shifts right while money supply is fixed. If the investment response to the interest-rate change is $50 billion and MPC = 0.75, what is the correct AD effect?
options: Money demand shifts right, r rises, investment falls, and AD decreases by $200 billion.
Money demand shifts right, r falls, investment rises, and AD increases by $200 billion.
Money supply shifts right, r falls, investment rises, and AD increases by $50 billion.
Money demand shifts left, r rises, investment falls, and AD decreases by $50 billion.
legendaryBoss.commonError: using the multiplier but reading the money-market movement backward
legendaryBoss.feedback: With fixed MS, higher MD raises r and lowers investment. MPC = 0.75 gives multiplier 4, so AD falls by $200 billion.

legendaryBoss.q: Money demand shifts left while money supply is fixed. If the investment response is $45 billion and MPC = 0.5, what is the correct AD effect?
options: MD shifts left, r falls, investment rises, and AD increases by $90 billion.
MD shifts left, r rises, investment falls, and AD decreases by $90 billion.
MD shifts right, r rises, investment falls, and AD decreases by $45 billion.
MD shifts right, r falls, investment rises, and AD increases by $45 billion.
legendaryBoss.commonError: claiming a price-level movement when the graph is a money-market shift
legendaryBoss.feedback: A leftward MD shift lowers r and raises investment. MPC 0.5 gives multiplier 2, so AD rises $90 billion.

legendaryBoss.q: The price level rises and shifts money demand right. The central bank wants to keep the interest rate unchanged. What action fits the model?
options: Decrease the money supply by selling securities.
Hold money supply fixed and require less investment.
Increase the money supply enough to match the higher money demand.
Shift aggregate supply left to reduce money demand.
legendaryBoss.commonError: Using contractionary policy to offset a rightward money-demand shift.
legendaryBoss.feedback: To prevent the interest rate from rising when money demand shifts right, the central bank must shift money supply right as well.

legendaryBoss.q: Refer to the money-market graph. With MD2 and MS2, point b is above the equilibrium interest rate at d. Which adjustment best explains movement toward equilibrium?
options: An excess supply of money leads people to buy interest-bearing assets, pushing the interest rate down toward r3.
An excess demand for money leads people to sell interest-bearing assets, lowering bond prices and pushing the interest rate farther above r4 until the central bank expands money supply.
Because MS2 is vertical, point b is an equilibrium regardless of money demand.
The central bank must shift MS2 left before any interest-rate adjustment can occur.
legendaryBoss.commonError: Treats a labeled point on a money-supply line as an equilibrium even when it is not on the active money-demand curve.
legendaryBoss.feedback: At an interest rate above equilibrium, money supplied exceeds money demanded and asset-market adjustment pushes the rate down; below equilibrium, excess money demand pushes it up.
legendaryBoss.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
legendaryBoss.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

legendaryBoss.q: Refer to the money-market graph. The economy moves from e to d because both money demand and money supply shift right. Which conclusion is supported by the final interest rate?
options: The supply shift dominates, because every increase in money supply raises the interest rate.
The two shifts exactly offset, because both curves move right.
Money demand must have shifted left, because the equilibrium quantity of money rises.
The demand shift dominates the supply shift’s interest-rate effect, because the equilibrium rate rises from r2 to r3.
legendaryBoss.commonError: Assumes the direction of one curve shift determines the interest rate even when both money demand and money supply move.
legendaryBoss.feedback: When money demand and money supply both shift, compare the new equilibrium with the old one; the interest-rate direction depends on their relative effects.
legendaryBoss.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
legendaryBoss.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

repairQuestions.q: In liquidity preference theory, the interest rate balances:
options: Money supply and money demand
Taxes and transfers
Exports and imports
Inflation and unemployment
repairQuestions.feedback: The interest rate adjusts to balance money supply and money demand.

repairQuestions.q: If money demand rises and money supply is fixed, the interest rate tends to:
options: Rise
Fall
Become zero
Become GDP
repairQuestions.feedback: Higher money demand pushes interest rates up when money supply is fixed.

repairQuestions.q: In the money market, the equilibrium interest rate occurs where:
options: Money demand equals money supply
AD equals SRAS
Saving equals investment only
Government spending equals taxes
repairQuestions.feedback: The money-market interest rate adjusts until the quantity of money demanded equals the quantity supplied.

repairQuestions.commonError: Calls an interest-rate-induced movement along a money-demand curve a shift of the curve.
repairQuestions.q: The central bank increases the money supply while income and the price level stay unchanged. The equilibrium interest rate falls. What happens to money demand in the standard diagram?
options: There is a movement down along the existing money-demand curve; the curve itself need not shift.
The money-demand curve shifts left because the lower interest rate changes households’ desired money holdings at every possible interest rate, not just at the new equilibrium.
The money-demand curve shifts right because the central bank supplied more money.
Money demand becomes vertical because the money supply changed.
repairQuestions.feedback: A change in the interest rate causes movement along a given money-demand curve. Income or the price level can shift the money-demand curve.

repairQuestions.commonError: Treats a labeled point on a money-supply line as an equilibrium even when it is not on the active money-demand curve.
repairQuestions.q: At the current interest rate, households want to hold more money than the fixed money supply provides. Which adjustment moves the market toward equilibrium?
options: People try to obtain money by selling interest-bearing assets, putting upward pressure on the interest rate.
People buy interest-bearing assets, pushing the interest rate downward.
The money-demand curve automatically shifts left until it equals money supply.
The central bank must change money supply because the interest rate cannot adjust.
repairQuestions.feedback: At an interest rate above equilibrium, money supplied exceeds money demanded and asset-market adjustment pushes the rate down; below equilibrium, excess money demand pushes it up.

repairQuestions.commonError: Reversing the effect of price level on money demand.
repairQuestions.q: When the price level rises, money demand usually:
options: Rises
Falls
Becomes zero
Turns into money supply
repairQuestions.feedback: Higher prices mean people need more money for transactions.

repairQuestions.commonError: Missing the investment step in the interest-rate effect.
repairQuestions.q: Higher interest rates tend to make investment:
options: Fall
Rise
Become government spending
Equal money demand
repairQuestions.feedback: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive, so investment falls.

bridgeQuestions.q: In the money market, if the interest rate is too low, quantity of money demanded is usually:
options: Greater than money supplied
Less than money supplied
Equal to zero
Equal to LRAS
bridgeQuestions.feedback: At too low an interest rate, people demand more money than is supplied, pushing rates up.

bridgeQuestions.q: Income rises, so people want to hold more money. If money supply is fixed, interest rates:
options: Rise
Fall
Become zero
Become inflation
bridgeQuestions.feedback: Higher money demand with fixed money supply raises interest rates.

bridgeQuestions.commonError: Confusing money-market and AD-AS equilibrium.
bridgeQuestions.q: Money demand shifts right while money supply is fixed. What happens to the interest rate?
options: It rises
It falls
It becomes zero
It turns into the price level
bridgeQuestions.feedback: With fixed money supply, higher money demand pushes the interest rate up.

bridgeQuestions.commonError: Stops after finding the new money-market interest rate and does not carry the result into spending and aggregate demand.
bridgeQuestions.q: A higher price level shifts money demand right while money supply is fixed, so the equilibrium interest rate rises. To carry that money-market result into the policy-transmission model, what happens next?
options: Interest-sensitive investment falls, putting downward pressure on aggregate demand.
Investment rises because higher rates make borrowing cheaper, shifting aggregate demand right.
Aggregate demand shifts left directly because the price level changed, with no spending channel involved.
The higher interest rate shifts money demand farther right but has no effect on spending.
bridgeQuestions.feedback: After solving the money market, use the interest-rate change to infer the direction of investment and other rate-sensitive spending, then the aggregate-demand shift.

bridgeQuestions.q: Money demand shifts right while money supply is fixed, raising the equilibrium interest rate. What is the next step if the student is bridging from the money market to monetary-policy transmission?
options: Higher borrowing costs reduce interest-sensitive investment and put downward pressure on aggregate demand.
Higher borrowing costs raise investment because firms earn more interest.
The higher interest rate directly increases government purchases.
Aggregate demand is unaffected because interest rates matter only inside the money-market graph.
bridgeQuestions.commonError: Stops after finding the new money-market interest rate and does not carry the result into spending and aggregate demand.
bridgeQuestions.feedback: After solving the money market, use the interest-rate change to infer the direction of investment and other rate-sensitive spending, then the aggregate-demand shift.

monetary-policy-transmission.title: Monetary-Policy Transmission
monetary-policy-transmission.description: Trace monetary policy through interest rates, investment, aggregate demand, and output.

easy.q: If the Fed increases the money supply, the interest rate usually:
options: Rises
Falls
Becomes the price level
Equals unemployment
easy.commonError: Reversing expansionary monetary policy.
easy.feedback: Increasing the money supply lowers the interest rate in the liquidity-preference model.

easy.q: If the Fed decreases the money supply, aggregate demand usually:
options: Shifts right
Shifts left
Becomes vertical
Turns into SRAS
easy.commonError: Reversing contractionary monetary policy.
easy.feedback: A lower money supply raises interest rates, reduces investment, and shifts AD left.

easy.q: Refer to the graph. Moving from MS1 to MS2 causes the interest rate to:
options: Rise from r1 to r2
Fall from r2 to r1
Stay at r1
Become the price level
easy.commonError: Reversing money supply shifts and interest rates.
easy.feedback: MS2 is left of MS1, so the money supply falls and the interest rate rises from r1 to r2.
easy.imageAlt: Two panels with vertical MS1 and MS2, downward MD, and downward AD1 and AD2.
easy.graphDescription: Left panel: interest rate r is on the vertical axis and money M on the horizontal axis. A downward-sloping MD curve intersects MS1 at r1; MS2 is left of MS1 and intersects MD at the higher rate r2. Right panel: price level P is on the vertical axis and output Y on the horizontal axis. AD2 lies left of AD1. At price level P1, output is Y1 on AD1 and Y2 on AD2.

easy.q: Refer to the graph. The move from AD1 to AD2 shows aggregate demand:
options: Shifting right
Shifting left
Becoming SRAS
Becoming LRAS
easy.commonError: Reversing AD shifts.
easy.feedback: AD2 is to the left of AD1, so aggregate demand decreases.
easy.imageAlt: Two panels with vertical MS1 and MS2, downward MD, and downward AD1 and AD2.
easy.graphDescription: Left panel: interest rate r is on the vertical axis and money M on the horizontal axis. A downward-sloping MD curve intersects MS1 at r1; MS2 is left of MS1 and intersects MD at the higher rate r2. Right panel: price level P is on the vertical axis and output Y on the horizontal axis. AD2 lies left of AD1. At price level P1, output is Y1 on AD1 and Y2 on AD2.

easy.q: If the Fed increases the money supply in the short run, interest rates tend to
options: fall
rise
stay fixed by Congress
become equal to inflation automatically
easy.commonError: thinking more money raises interest rates in the liquidity preference model
easy.feedback: An increase in money supply lowers the equilibrium interest rate in the liquidity preference model.

easy.q: If the Fed decreases the money supply in the short run, interest rates tend to
options: rise
fall
turn negative automatically
stop affecting investment
easy.commonError: thinking less money lowers interest rates
easy.feedback: A decrease in money supply raises the equilibrium interest rate.

easy.q: Lower interest rates tend to make investment spending
options: increase
decrease
stay unchanged by definition
equal money demand
easy.commonError: thinking lower borrowing costs reduce investment
easy.feedback: Lower interest rates make borrowing cheaper, so investment spending tends to increase.

easy.q: Higher interest rates tend to make investment spending
options: decrease
increase
equal consumption
shift money supply right
easy.commonError: thinking higher borrowing costs increase investment
easy.feedback: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive, so investment spending tends to decrease.

easy.q: Expansionary monetary policy usually shifts aggregate demand
options: right
left
nowhere because AD cannot shift
down along the same curve only
easy.commonError: confusing a shift in AD with a movement along AD
easy.feedback: Expansionary monetary policy lowers interest rates, raises investment, and shifts AD right.

easy.q: Contractionary monetary policy usually shifts aggregate demand
options: left
right
up along short-run aggregate supply
only through the labor market
easy.commonError: thinking tighter money increases aggregate demand
easy.feedback: Contractionary monetary policy raises interest rates, reduces investment, and shifts AD left.

easy.q: A liquidity trap occurs when monetary policy may lose power because nominal interest rates are near
options: zero
100 percent
the reserve ratio
the unemployment rate
easy.commonError: thinking liquidity traps happen when inflation is high by itself
easy.feedback: A liquidity trap occurs when interest rates are near zero, limiting the central bank's ability to lower them further.

easy.q: The left panel shows money supply increasing from MS0 to MS1. What happens to the nominal interest rate?
options: It rises from 4 percent to 6 percent
It stays at 6 percent
It falls from 6 percent to 4 percent
It falls from 6 percent to 2 percent
easy.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
easy.feedback: The increase in money supply moves the money-market equilibrium from A at 6 percent to B at 4 percent.
easy.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
easy.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (100,6) and dashed MS1 at B (150,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and upper dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (100,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (125,56.25). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

easy.q: In the contractionary two-panel diagram, what happens to the nominal interest rate after the money-supply change?
options: It rises from 2.75 percent to 4 percent
It falls from 4 percent to 2.75 percent
It stays at 2.75 percent
It rises from 4 percent to 6 percent
easy.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
easy.feedback: The smaller money supply moves equilibrium from A at 2.75 percent to B at 4 percent.
easy.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
easy.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (125,2.75) and dashed MS1 at B (100,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and lower dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (125,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (100,45). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

medium.q: Refer to the money-market graph. If the Fed moves from MS1 to MS2, the policy is:
options: Expansionary monetary policy
Contractionary monetary policy
Expansionary fiscal policy
A positive supply shock
medium.commonError: Reversing leftward money-supply shifts.
medium.feedback: MS2 is left of MS1, so the money supply falls and interest rates rise.
medium.imageAlt: Two panels with vertical MS1 and MS2, downward MD, and downward AD1 and AD2.
medium.graphDescription: Left panel: interest rate r is on the vertical axis and money M on the horizontal axis. A downward-sloping MD curve intersects MS1 at r1; MS2 is left of MS1 and intersects MD at the higher rate r2. Right panel: price level P is on the vertical axis and output Y on the horizontal axis. AD2 lies left of AD1. At price level P1, output is Y1 on AD1 and Y2 on AD2.

medium.q: Refer to the money-market and AD graph. The move from MS1 to MS2 leads to:
options: Lower r and higher AD
Higher r and lower AD
Higher r and higher AD
Lower r and lower AD
medium.commonError: Breaking the interest-rate to AD chain.
medium.feedback: A lower money supply raises r, reducing investment and shifting AD left.
medium.imageAlt: Two panels with vertical MS1 and MS2, downward MD, and downward AD1 and AD2.
medium.graphDescription: Left panel: interest rate r is on the vertical axis and money M on the horizontal axis. A downward-sloping MD curve intersects MS1 at r1; MS2 is left of MS1 and intersects MD at the higher rate r2. Right panel: price level P is on the vertical axis and output Y on the horizontal axis. AD2 lies left of AD1. At price level P1, output is Y1 on AD1 and Y2 on AD2.

medium.q: What is the correct short-run chain from an increase in the money supply to aggregate demand?
options: Money supply rises, interest rates fall, investment rises, AD shifts right.
Money supply rises, interest rates rise, investment falls, AD shifts left.
Money supply rises, taxes rise, consumption falls, AD shifts left.
Money supply rises, reserve requirements rise, AD disappears.
medium.commonError: reversing the interest-rate effect
medium.feedback: Expansionary monetary policy lowers interest rates, raises investment, and shifts AD right.

medium.q: What is the correct short-run chain from a decrease in the money supply to aggregate demand?
options: Money supply falls, interest rates rise, investment falls, AD shifts left.
Money supply falls, interest rates fall, investment rises, AD shifts right.
Money supply falls, taxes fall, consumption rises, AD shifts right.
Money supply falls, MPC rises, AD shifts right.
medium.commonError: thinking tighter money lowers interest rates
medium.feedback: Contractionary monetary policy raises interest rates, reduces investment, and shifts AD left.

medium.q: Refer to the graph. Which panel represents the money market part of the monetary policy transmission mechanism?
options: The panel with money supply, money demand, and the interest rate
The panel with aggregate demand and output only
The panel with government spending only
The panel with the money multiplier only
medium.commonError: confusing the money market graph with the AD graph
medium.feedback: The money market panel shows money supply, money demand, and the interest rate.
medium.imageAlt: Two panels with vertical MS1 and MS2, downward MD, and downward AD1 and AD2.
medium.graphDescription: Left panel: interest rate r is on the vertical axis and money M on the horizontal axis. A downward-sloping MD curve intersects MS1 at r1; MS2 is left of MS1 and intersects MD at the higher rate r2. Right panel: price level P is on the vertical axis and output Y on the horizontal axis. AD2 lies left of AD1. At price level P1, output is Y1 on AD1 and Y2 on AD2.

medium.q: In the monetary policy transmission mechanism, a lower interest rate leads most directly to
options: higher investment spending
lower investment spending
lower government spending automatically
a smaller money supply automatically
medium.commonError: thinking lower borrowing costs reduce investment
medium.feedback: Lower interest rates make borrowing cheaper, so investment spending rises.

medium.q: If the Fed increases the money supply, the aggregate demand curve should
options: shift right
shift left
become vertical
turn into money demand
medium.commonError: confusing movement along AD with a shift of AD
medium.feedback: More money lowers interest rates, raises investment, and shifts AD right.

medium.q: A liquidity trap limits traditional monetary policy because
options: nominal interest rates cannot be pushed much below zero
money demand is always zero
government spending cannot change
banks cannot hold reserves
medium.commonError: thinking the Fed can always lower nominal rates without limit
medium.feedback: When nominal rates are near zero, the Fed has less room to stimulate spending through further rate cuts.

medium.q: If the economy is weak and the Fed wants to stimulate aggregate demand, which action fits the goal?
options: Increase the money supply to lower interest rates.
Decrease the money supply to raise interest rates.
Raise taxes to reduce consumption.
Lower government spending to reduce AD.
medium.commonError: choosing contractionary money during weak demand
medium.feedback: To stimulate AD, the Fed can increase the money supply, lower interest rates, and encourage investment.

medium.q: If inflation pressure is high because aggregate demand is too strong, which Fed action fits the goal?
options: Decrease the money supply to raise interest rates.
Increase the money supply to lower interest rates.
Buy bonds to increase investment.
Cut interest rates to shift AD right.
medium.commonError: using expansionary monetary policy when AD is already too high
medium.feedback: To cool AD, the Fed can reduce the money supply, raise interest rates, and reduce investment.

medium.q: Which aggregate-demand change accompanies the lower interest rate in the right panel?
options: AD shifts left from AD1 to AD0
SRAS shifts right while AD stays fixed
LRAS shifts left
AD shifts right from AD0 to AD1
medium.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
medium.feedback: The lower interest rate stimulates interest-sensitive spending, shifting aggregate demand right.
medium.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
medium.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (100,6) and dashed MS1 at B (150,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and upper dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (100,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (125,56.25). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

medium.q: In the expansionary two-panel diagram, how many units does real GDP rise from A to B?
medium.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
medium.feedback: Read real GDP at A and B: 125 − 100 = 25 units.
medium.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
medium.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (100,6) and dashed MS1 at B (150,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and upper dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (100,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (125,56.25). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

medium.q: In the right panel, which aggregate-demand change accompanies the higher interest rate generated on the left?
options: AD shifts right from AD1 to AD0
AD shifts left from AD0 to AD1
SRAS shifts left while AD stays fixed
LRAS shifts right
medium.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
medium.feedback: The higher interest rate reduces interest-sensitive spending, shifting aggregate demand left.
medium.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
medium.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (125,2.75) and dashed MS1 at B (100,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and lower dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (125,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (100,45). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

medium.q: In the contractionary two-panel diagram, how many units does real GDP fall from A to B?
medium.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
medium.feedback: Read real GDP at A and B: 125 − 100 = 25 units.
medium.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
medium.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (125,2.75) and dashed MS1 at B (100,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and lower dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (125,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (100,45). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

hard.q: Refer to the money-market graph. Which movement shows contractionary monetary policy with MD1 unchanged?
options: g to e
e to g
a to d
d to a
hard.commonError: Reversing a leftward money supply shift.
hard.feedback: Contractionary policy shifts MS left from MS2 to MS1, moving from g to e on MD1.
hard.imageAlt: Money-market graph with two vertical money-supply curves and two downward-sloping money-demand curves.
hard.graphDescription: The vertical axis is interest rate r and the horizontal axis is quantity of money Qm. MS1 is vertical at Qm1 and MS2 is vertical to its right at Qm2. MD1 slopes downward through e at Qm1, r2 and g at Qm2, r1. MD2 is shifted right/up and slopes downward through a at Qm1, r4 and d at Qm2, r3. Additional labeled points are b at Qm2, r4; c at Qm1, r3; and f at Qm1, r1.

hard.q: Refer to the money-market and AD graph. A fall from r2 to r1 is associated with:
options: MS rising and AD shifting right
MS falling and AD shifting left
MD rising and AD shifting left
MD falling and SRAS shifting left
hard.commonError: Breaking the r-to-AD link.
hard.feedback: A higher money supply lowers r, raises investment, and shifts AD right.
hard.imageAlt: Two panels with vertical MS1 and MS2, downward MD, and downward AD1 and AD2.
hard.graphDescription: Left panel: interest rate r is on the vertical axis and money M on the horizontal axis. A downward-sloping MD curve intersects MS1 at r1; MS2 is left of MS1 and intersects MD at the higher rate r2. Right panel: price level P is on the vertical axis and output Y on the horizontal axis. AD2 lies left of AD1. At price level P1, output is Y1 on AD1 and Y2 on AD2.

hard.q: A central bank wants to close a recessionary AD gap without fiscal policy. Which chain is most accurate?
options: Buy bonds, lower rates, raise investment, shift AD right
Sell bonds, lower rates, raise investment, shift AD right
Buy bonds, raise rates, reduce investment, shift AD left
Sell bonds, raise rates, raise investment, shift AD left
hard.commonError: Reversing the monetary transmission chain.
hard.feedback: Expansionary monetary policy buys bonds, increases money supply, lowers rates, raises investment, and shifts AD right.

hard.q: Which chain best explains expansionary monetary policy in the short run?
options: Fed buys bonds, money supply rises, interest rate falls, investment rises, AD shifts right.
Fed sells bonds, money supply rises, interest rate falls, investment rises, AD shifts right.
Fed buys bonds, money supply falls, interest rate rises, investment falls, AD shifts left.
Fed raises taxes, money demand falls, investment rises, AD shifts right.
hard.commonError: confusing bond purchases with bond sales
hard.feedback: Buying bonds increases money supply, lowers interest rates, raises investment, and shifts AD right.

hard.q: Which chain best explains contractionary monetary policy in the short run?
options: Fed sells bonds, money supply falls, interest rate rises, investment falls, AD shifts left.
Fed buys bonds, money supply falls, interest rate rises, investment falls, AD shifts left.
Fed sells bonds, money supply rises, interest rate falls, investment rises, AD shifts right.
Fed cuts taxes, interest rates rise, AD shifts left.
hard.commonError: thinking Fed bond sales expand the money supply
hard.feedback: Selling bonds reduces money supply, raises interest rates, lowers investment, and shifts AD left.

hard.q: If the Fed reduces the money supply, which sequence is most likely?
options: Money supply shifts left, interest rates rise, and AD shifts left.
Money supply shifts right, interest rates fall, and AD shifts right.
Money demand shifts left, interest rates fall, and AD shifts right.
Money supply shifts left, interest rates fall, and AD shifts right.
hard.commonError: reversing the interest-rate effect of lower money supply
hard.feedback: A lower money supply raises interest rates, reduces investment, and shifts AD left.

hard.q: If the Fed increases money supply, which sequence is most likely?
options: Money supply shifts right, interest rates fall, and AD shifts right.
Money supply shifts left, interest rates rise, and AD shifts left.
Money demand shifts right, interest rates rise, and AD shifts left.
Money supply shifts right, interest rates rise, and AD shifts left.
hard.commonError: thinking more money raises interest rates in liquidity preference theory
hard.feedback: A higher money supply lowers interest rates, raises investment, and shifts AD right.

hard.q: Why might monetary policy be weak in a liquidity trap?
options: Interest rates are near zero, so further traditional rate cuts are limited.
Money demand is always upward sloping.
Fiscal policy stops affecting AD.
The money supply cannot be changed by any central bank.
hard.commonError: thinking central banks can always lower nominal rates without limit
hard.feedback: When nominal rates are near zero, the usual interest-rate channel has less room to operate.

hard.q: A stock market crash reduces household wealth and aggregate demand. Which Fed response best stabilizes output?
options: Increase money supply and lower interest rates.
Decrease money supply and raise interest rates.
Raise taxes and lower government spending.
Sell bonds to reduce investment.
hard.commonError: choosing contractionary policy after a negative demand shock
hard.feedback: A negative AD shock calls for expansionary monetary policy if the goal is stabilizing output.

hard.q: An economy is overheating because aggregate demand is too high. Which Fed response best reduces inflation pressure?
options: Reduce money supply and raise interest rates.
Increase money supply and lower interest rates.
Buy bonds to raise investment.
Lower reserve requirements to shift AD right.
hard.commonError: stimulating AD when AD is already excessive
hard.feedback: To reduce inflation pressure from excessive AD, the Fed can tighten money and raise interest rates.

hard.q: Which sequence matches the changes from point A to point B across the two panels?
options: MS ↑ → rate ↑ → spending ↓ → AD ← → output and price level ↓
MS ↑ → rate ↓ → spending ↑ → AD → → output and price level ↑
MS ↓ → rate ↓ → spending ↑ → AD → → output and price level ↑
MD ↑ → rate ↓ → spending ↑ → SRAS → → output and price level ↓
hard.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
hard.feedback: That is the standard expansionary monetary-policy transmission chain represented by the two panels.
hard.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
hard.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (100,6) and dashed MS1 at B (150,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and upper dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (100,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (125,56.25). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

hard.q: Which causal chain matches the changes from A to B in the second two-panel diagram?
options: MS ↓ → rate ↓ → spending ↑ → AD → → output and price level ↑
MS ↑ → rate ↑ → spending ↓ → AD ← → output and price level ↓
MD ↓ → rate ↑ → spending ↓ → SRAS ← → output and price level ↑
MS ↓ → rate ↑ → spending ↓ → AD ← → output and price level ↓
hard.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
hard.feedback: That is the standard contractionary monetary-policy transmission chain shown across the two panels.
hard.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
hard.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (125,2.75) and dashed MS1 at B (100,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and lower dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (125,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (100,45). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

elite.q: Refer to the money-market and AD graph. Which chain correctly explains the movement shown from MS1 to MS2 and AD1 to AD2?
options: Money supply falls, r rises, investment falls, AD falls
Money supply rises, r falls, investment falls, AD falls
Money demand falls, r rises, consumption rises, AD rises
Money supply falls, r falls, investment rises, AD rises
elite.commonError: Breaking the monetary transmission chain.
elite.feedback: A lower money supply raises interest rates, reduces investment, and shifts AD left.
elite.imageAlt: Two panels with vertical MS1 and MS2, downward MD, and downward AD1 and AD2.
elite.graphDescription: Left panel: interest rate r is on the vertical axis and money M on the horizontal axis. A downward-sloping MD curve intersects MS1 at r1; MS2 is left of MS1 and intersects MD at the higher rate r2. Right panel: price level P is on the vertical axis and output Y on the horizontal axis. AD2 lies left of AD1. At price level P1, output is Y1 on AD1 and Y2 on AD2.

elite.q: If the Fed shifts money supply right, which chain correctly reaches aggregate demand?
options: MS rises, r falls, investment rises, AD shifts right.
MS rises, r rises, investment falls, AD shifts left.
MS falls, r falls, investment rises, AD shifts right.
MD rises, r rises, investment rises, AD shifts right.
elite.commonError: reversing the effect of money supply on interest rates
elite.feedback: More money lowers the interest rate, raises investment, and shifts AD right.

elite.q: If the Fed shifts money supply left, which chain correctly reaches aggregate demand?
options: MS falls, r rises, investment falls, AD shifts left.
MS falls, r falls, investment rises, AD shifts right.
MS rises, r rises, investment falls, AD shifts left.
MD falls, r rises, investment falls, AD shifts left.
elite.commonError: thinking less money lowers interest rates
elite.feedback: Less money raises the interest rate, lowers investment, and shifts AD left.

elite.q: If the Fed increases money supply but investment barely responds to the lower interest rate, what happens to the AD shift?
options: AD shifts right by less than usual because the investment channel is weak.
AD shifts right by more because investment does not matter.
AD must shift left because lower r reduces investment.
AD cannot move because money supply changed.
elite.commonError: assuming the money-supply shift mechanically creates the same AD response every time
elite.feedback: Monetary policy works through investment. If investment barely responds, AD shifts right less.

elite.q: If the economy is in a liquidity trap, which part of the normal expansionary monetary-policy chain weakens?
options: The ability of extra money to lower r enough to boost investment
The identity that AD includes investment
The fact that money demand exists
The ability of government spending to enter AD
elite.commonError: thinking liquidity trap means money demand disappears
elite.feedback: In a liquidity trap, additional money may not lower interest rates enough to stimulate investment.

elite.q: If money supply rises and AD shifts right, what is the correct distinction between the money-market movement and the AD-AS outcome?
options: The money market shows r falling; the AD-AS model shows higher demand for output at each price level.
The money market shows P falling; the AD-AS model shows money demand disappearing.
The money market shows taxes falling; the AD-AS model shows reserves rising.
The money market shows real output fixed by bank reserves.
elite.commonError: blending the money-market graph and AD graph into one axis system
elite.feedback: The money market determines the interest rate. The AD-AS model then reflects how lower rates raise spending and shift AD.

elite.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes what changes in the two panels?
options: MD shifts right and MS is traversed; SRAS shifts right along fixed AD.
MS shifts left and MD is traversed; AD shifts left along fixed SRAS.
MS shifts right and MD is traversed; AD shifts right along fixed SRAS.
Both panels show movements along fixed demand and supply curves.
elite.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
elite.feedback: Different markets are being linked. Money supply shifts first; the resulting rate change affects spending and shifts AD.
elite.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
elite.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (100,6) and dashed MS1 at B (150,4). Right panel axes: real GDP horizontally and price level vertically. Solid AD0 and upper dashed AD1 slope downward; red SRAS slopes upward. AD0 meets SRAS at A (100,50); AD1 meets SRAS at B (125,56.25). Dashed horizontal and vertical guides mark those coordinates.

elite.q: A student says AD1 is lower because the central bank directly reduced real GDP. What is the better interpretation?
options: Lower MS raises rates; lower interest-sensitive spending shifts AD left.
Lower MS lowers rates; higher interest-sensitive spending shifts AD right.
The central bank directly sets real GDP and moves AD to that quantity.
A rightward MD shift raises rates and directly shifts SRAS to the left.
elite.commonError: misreads_money_market_or_transmission
elite.feedback: Monetary policy works through a transmission mechanism. The central bank acts on money/financial conditions, which influence spending and AD.
elite.imageAlt: Two panels with MD0 and vertical MS0 and MS1 on the left and AD0, AD1 and SRAS on the right.
elite.graphDescription: Left panel axes: quantity of money horizontally and nominal interest rate (%) vertically. Downward MD0 meets solid MS0 at A (125,2.75) and dashed MS1 at B (100,4).
